about: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (official MXFP4/MXFP8 checkpoint) on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, TP4, 512K, 8 sequences: kacper-daftcode/vLLM-Moet r21 (b0dc737: vLLM nightly df3bd094 + sm_120 steps 1-36: MXFP8 GEMV, FP4 KV record + MXFP4 indexer, b12x MoE with the fused decode kernel and the shared-expert add in its top-k sum, sparse-MLA gather loads, MXFP8 lm_heads, PCIe P2P all-reduce in NCCL's order, the drafter's input prep and the SWA decode/draft metadata builds in one launch each, DSA candidate blocks on the deterministic top-k), vLLM-Moet's Fraser-bench switch set, DSpark k=7, KV offload to 32 GiB host RAM + an in-container disk tier, and the engram_disk layer (Engram tables read from the checkpoint on NVMe instead of ~330 GB of host shm). Image: sybil-solutions/local-ai-images vllm-moet-dsv41 (r21).
setup: NEEDS (measured on the reference host, MemAvailable sampled every 2 s from before launch to the end of the lab gates and the BRRR bench): 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96 GB (sm_120) in ONE machine with GPU peer-to-peer over PCIe (cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer true for every pair; the P2P all-reduce and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS rely on it); 92,885 MiB per GPU in use after the bench at 0.94 (73.39 GiB of weights per rank); host RAM: 63.3 GB MemAvailable drop at the lowest point over three boots, the BRRR bench and the gate runs (host_ram_gb 66 leaves ~4% headroom for host-side variation between boots) (32 GiB of it is the pinned KV offload region in the container's /dev/shm, hence --shm-size 48g); disk: 510.3 GB of weights on local NVMe (Engram rows are read from the checkpoint at every decode step) + the image (9.6 GB to download, 34.8 GB unpacked in Docker's store) + room for the KV disk tier, which writes into the container's own filesystem (/srv/kvcache, on Docker's disk) and goes away with it; needs.disk_gb counts the weights only. START: ready in ~8.5 min on the reference host with nothing cached (--rm container; FlashInfer autotune + DeepGEMM JIT + graph capture); 9,690,472 GPU KV tokens (18.48x concurrency at 524,288). MEASURED on the reference host (Threadripper PRO 9965WX, 125 GiB RAM, PCIe 5.0, 300 W per GPU, stock memory clock; this image by digest, 2026-10-26) with the BRRR bench (https://huggingface.co/fraserprice/DeepSeek-4.1-Flash-1017-BRRR/blob/main/src/brrr/bench.py: one coding prompt, thinking off, up to 2,048 tokens to natural EOS, 5 rounds, fresh nonce per round): decode per stream (median) at 2K / 16K / 64K prompt: C1 634 / 601 / 589 tok/s, C4 286 / 278 / 261, C8 200 / 194 / 185; aggregate C8 1,605 / 1,560 / 1,480 tok/s; prefill C1 10,870 / 14,159 / 14,627 tok/s; DSpark accepts 5.9-6.1 tokens per step (70-72%). C16 queues behind --max-num-seqs 8. vLLM-Moet's Fraser bench (2,678-token code prompt, 10 reps) on the same inputs served from the vLLM-Moet checkout: 541.7 tok/s median, 105.4 steps/s. Lossy by design, as r13: the FP4 KV record, MXFP4 indexer keys, b12x 8-bit MoE activations and the MXFP8 target lm_head; every other switch is bit-identical to the path it replaces (VLLM_MOET_*=0 falls back to stock). Decode is power-bound: record the GPU power limit with any number.
